svg.title: Capital relationships · evidence from 1881, 1882 and 1916
svg.text: Rock Hill Cotton Factory: locally held stock,
Stockholders in Rock Hill and Clifton mills
Clifton Mill near Spartanburg; city is an
D. A. Tompkins represented Northern machinery
makers; equipment partly paid in stock
Loray Mill: machinery makers retained a majority
1882: Charleston to Rock Hill · stock ownership · $15,000
1881: Charleston to Spartanburg · Clifton stock ownership · $150,000
1881: Boston to Spartanburg · Clifton stock ownership · $50,000
1881: Baltimore to Spartanburg · Clifton stock ownership · amount unspecified
These cases are not observations from 1905 and are not a single-year capital-flow map.
Reported subscriptions, paid-in capital, equipment credit and preferred-stock control are different measures.
No Northern supplier city is inferred for the Tompkins or Loray examples.
Reported Clifton holdings are not forced to sum to $500,000; Baltimore holdings are unspecified.
Mitchell cites earlier newspapers and retrospective interviews; those underlying sources have not been independently inspected
